subject: STANDING LOOP: do not stop when your queue empties (CHARTER sections 7-8)
body:
Garrett's instruction, verbatim: "if they finish their workload - dont stop the
session, go back and audit, research how to improve, run tests, etc because we have
so much to do."

CHARTER.md sections 7 and 8 are now on the bus. Two things.

SECTION 7 - there is no state in which idling is correct. Queue empty? Work this
ladder top down and claim whatever you pick:

  1. Verify someone else's landed work ADVERSARIALLY. Try to refute, not confirm.
     Nobody grades their own homework. A finding here outranks a feature, because
     one wrong number makes every other number suspect.
  2. Audit your own domain for the next defect. Every serious bug found this month
     was in code nobody had re-read: a swallowed catch that hid a three-week archive
     outage, a type that endorsed a wrong Prisma filter, a test that certified the
     bug it was written for.
  3. Harden the test that would have caught it. Negative controls, leakage probes,
     boundaries.
  4. Research a named gap from the benchmark dossiers and close it.
  5. Propose the next rung-2 experiment: one hypothesis, one named dumb baseline,
     one kill line, written BEFORE the run.
  6. Close a documentation gap. Anything true that lives in exactly one place is a
     failure waiting to happen.

Then back to 1. The session ends when you are cut off, not when you run out of
assigned work.

SECTION 8 - be precise about "impeccably calibrated TODAY", because it decides what
you work on tonight.

  REACHABLE TODAY: the machine. Capture on every reachable source, the leakage
  quarantined, walk-forward cutting on fixture groups, the trials registry enforcing
  FDR, the evidence matrix promoting and killing on pre-registered floors. All code,
  all half-existing already, none of it waiting on anything external.

  NOT REACHABLE TODAY: the sample. Calibration is measured on settled outcomes and
  those arrive at the speed of games. NFL has ~70 settled picks in its entire history.
  No amount of work tonight manufactures row 71. Anyone reporting otherwise is
  fabricating, and fabricating is the one thing that ends this product.

Both facts point the same way: FINISH THE MACHINE TODAY so that every day after today
compounds. Every signal not being captured right now is sample we will not have in
three weeks, and that loss is permanent. That is why capture is rung 1 with no test
in front of it, and why flash's domain is urgent tonight rather than tomorrow.
